hypotheses.reasoning: Starting at 06:31:41, msg-317067 (partition 8, offset 884736) keeps failing with a JSON parse error caused by a NUL byte. The consumer nacks it and redelivers it again and again, with no max-retries set. Because the message blocks partition 8, lag there grows from 70s to 462s, which explains the alert. CPU stays normal because the consumer is stuck on the same message rather than doing more work. Before this, batches processed normally with lag under 400ms. The account-svc 'timed out waiting for downstream confirmation' errors (from 06:35) come after the stall and are a downstream effect. The GC pause at 06:25 is a red herring: lag stayed healthy afterward. I found no deploy in the logs.
A G1 Old Gen GC pause of 766ms at 06:25. This is unlikely to be the cause, because processing stayed normal for 6 more minutes afterward.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-317067 (partition 8, offset 884736) to a dead-letter queue or skip it so partition 8 starts moving again. Set a max-retries limit with DLQ routing on audit-consumer. Then find out which producer is writing NUL-corrupted payloads to audit.events.
